name: Power

sections.body:
A dependable grid frees cooking, lighting and workshop labor from a dwindling emergency fuel stock. Generate current, connect the buildings that need it and store enough to keep essential services running through darkness or poor wind.

Water collection and electrical generation serve different needs. A sand turbine resembles a windtrap in its need for open air, but its output is electricity.
sections.title: Current for the sietch

sections.body:
Sietch electrics unlocks the power leads and switches used to connect generators, storage and workstations. Glowglobes provide electric light; powered cooking and tailoring can take over routine work once supply is dependable.

Keep major loads in view when expanding. Cultivation lights demand far more current than a small workshop, and an exhausted fuel-cell can leave several essential jobs waiting at once.
sections.title: Power leads and glowglobes

sections.body:
Compact sun-cells produce up to 850 W in daylight, while sun arrays reach 2,000 W. They stop at night and cannot collect beneath a roof. Sand turbines reach 1,600 W and larger arrays 2,800 W as wind permits; obstructed or enclosed siting reduces their usefulness.

A mature sietch can build a 3,000 W fusion cell for continuous generation without a carried fuel supply. Its expense makes solar and wind the usual early investment.
sections.title: Sun, wind and fusion

sections.body:
Plasteel fuel-cells store electricity for the night and for interruptions in generation. Each household cell holds 600 Wd and has 50% charging efficiency. A charged cell is a reserve that can be spent, not an independent generator.

Protect storage from rain and fire, which can cause shorts. Build enough generation to recharge the reserve as well as operate daytime equipment.
sections.title: Plasteel fuel-cells

sections.body:
A steam vent can support a deep-vent plant producing 3,600 W and a substantial flow of sealed water rations. The vent fixes where the plant can be built, making a suitable site valuable to both industry and water supply.

Vents are rare. Plan ordinary settlement water around windtraps rather than assuming every colony will find a vent close to shelter.
sections.title: Deep-vent plants

patches.purpose: Converts grid/lights and hides Core temperate producers

summary: Sun-cells, sand turbines and stored current power the sietch. Rare steam vents and costly fusion plants support heavier industry when daylight alone is no longer enough.
